title: Winter Storm
description: Use this list before winter and when a Winter Storm Watch is issued, so you can stay warm and safe through snow, ice, and power loss.

sources.title: Winter Storms Aren't Over: CPSC Warns of Deadly Carbon Monoxide Risks and Fires During Power Outages

items.text: Install battery or battery-backup carbon monoxide alarms on every level and outside sleeping areas, and test them
Never use a generator, grill, camp stove, or charcoal indoors, in a garage, or on a porch; never heat with a gas oven
Keep snow cleared from furnace, dryer, and water heater vents
Extra blankets, sleeping bags, hats, and warm layers for everyone
Several days of water, no-cook food, and medicines
Flashlights and batteries (not candles) and a battery or hand-crank radio
Plan one warm room: interior, few windows, doors closed, towels under doors
Know where the nearest warming center is and go before night if the home gets too cold
Space heaters: at least 3 feet (1 m) from anything that can burn, plugged straight into the wall, never left on unattended
Know the alerts: Watch means a storm is possible; Warning means heavy snow or ice is expected - stay off roads
Insulate exposed pipes and know where the main water shutoff is
Learn signs of frostbite (numb, white or waxy skin) and hypothermia (shivering, confusion, slurred speech) - call 911 for confusion
If you heat with wood, stock dry firewood and have the chimney checked
Charge phones and power banks before the storm
Ice melt or sand and a snow shovel; push snow instead of lifting and take breaks to protect your heart
Keep the car's gas tank full and a winter car kit inside
Stay out from under ice-loaded trees and treat every downed line as live
Check on older neighbors and people living alone
If pipes freeze, warm them with a hair dryer or warm towels - never an open flame
Boots with good tread for walking on ice
